doc.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021

title: How titles arrive
summary: Israels says titles come arbitrarily, sometimes before the piece; Rowe mentions Braxton's diagram titles.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. I think I knew the answer to that from what you have said earlier. So really thank you for your time. I have one last quick question, when do titles arrive for you when you composes?

Sometimes before the piece, sometimes there’s a list of them and I just stick one on. Because they mostly, it’s pretty hard to describe. It could be Composition #1, Composition #3, Composition #47 so the answer is they come kind of arbitrarily. I’ve got to give it a name. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
Right. It needs a name. Who was the sax player who would have diagrams and — Anthony Braxton. Sometimes he would have like little drawings and stuff, that was the title.
Uh huh. Well I can understand that.
Okay. Well I appreciate your time today and it was a fascinating conversation. I wish you best of luck that your nonet continues and that you continue composing and so forth.
